items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: his concert master was a student of mine, Knoel Scott. I had him for four years at State University of New York in Old Westbury.

ctx.x: Did you ever have an association with Sun Ra?

Yes. Yes, yes, yes. Sun Ra was from Chicago. And a lot of my friends still play with Sun Ra. Some of my students, in fact his concert master was a student of mine, Knoel Scott. I had him for four years at State University of New York in Old Westbury. In fact Sun Ra was playing in my studio. He was rehearsing there. And a lot of these guys joined his band just because they hung out at my studio and were around when he was rehearsing. He said, “Well I don’t have a flute player today. Oh you play the flute? Get on…

most — well I won’t say most, but a lot of his musicians, he always had a big open house, would actually wind up living there with him. And you know, having family and whatnot I could never devote that kind of outside, time outside of my family. But I remember the last time I played with Sun Ra he was working at a club down in Greenwich Village called the Bottom Line. And the club is not there anymore. I mean the building is there but the club is different. And at one point he had us all marching around the club…
